title: It Didn’t, or Doesn’t, Matter
content: Yesterday seemed like a relatively routine day in the stock market.  Sure, stocks closed lower, but the magnitude of the decline was quite modest relative to the macroeconomic backdrop that prevailed.  On a day when 10-year yields rose by 12 basis points and crude oil futures jumped by more than 6%, a downward move in SPX of 0.58% wasn’t a bad result. That loss was recovered in the pre-market before a higher-than-expected CPI print had us off to the races.

title: Diesel at an All-Time High as Washington Buys a 35% Stake in Venezuela’s Oilfields
content:
If you filled up your tank this Labor Day weekend, you ended up paying the highest gas prices ever for this time of year.

The national average hit $4.15 per gallon during the holiday, an approximately 30% increase from last year, according to AAA. What’s more, August was the first month in history where the national average never dipped below $4 on a given day.
